newsitem.title: CHINA: China premier says Sino-UK ties on mend.
newsitem.headline: China premier says Sino-UK ties on mend.

text.p: Chinese Premier Li Peng has said that Sino-British ties are improving after past friction, the official Xinhua news agency reported.

Hong Kong was still the most important problem between Britain and China and the two nations should try to avoid new strains over the territory, Li said according to a Xinhua report issued late on Wednesday.
The Premier made the remarks in a meeting on Wednesday with Ian Lang, president of Britain's Board of Trade.
"After a period of twists and turns, there emerges a trend for improvement in Sino-British relations, which have embarked on a track for normal growth," Xinhua quoted the Premier as saying.
China and Britain have sparred over Hong Kong, which reverts to Beijing rule on July 1, 1997.
Beijing has been angered by Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten's drive to expand democracy in the colony ahead of the transfer of power.
"There are only 300 days before the return of Hong Kong to the motherland and the return is irreversible," Li said.
"Therefore, China and Britain should strengthen cooperation and avoid new trouble in order to ensure the smooth transfer of power of Hong Kong to China, which is in the interests of both countries."
Beijing wanted to expand trade, and British companies had a competitive edge in energy, communications, chemicals telecommunications and aviation, according to Li.
Lang was quoted as saying that the British government and business companies were satisfied with the improvement in ties and wanted more cooperation with China.
